evidence:
REACHABILITY: no unreachable item found. Runtime: environment/Dockerfile:9-12 installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH (line 3); tests/Dockerfile pins the same two versions, so 'don't install packages' (instruction.md:15) is satisfiable in both images. Seed: seed_data.json has 7 users whose emails/roles/tiers match instruction.md:19 and app_context.md, 3 employees, constants and reference_moment 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z; the one DRAFT row cited by hireops_rules.md:215 exists (status counts COMMITTED 8, PENDING 4, DRAFT 1). Passwords are given in the brief. Operational rows are explicitly optional (instruction.md:17, rules:91-95) and the functional prompt builds its own controls (functional/prompt.md:27). The live desk needs only polling/SSE/sockets (rules:532-533), browser storage and one sign-out path; nothing needs an outside service. Scripted golden observations (live-desk.json, hash verified, not a configured judge run) show every change-desk behaviour achieved by the reference in this runtime. I recomputed the B1/D1 worked figures from rules sections 2 and 11 (run-rates 100.00, basis 105.01->104.02 and 105.01->106.03, adjustments -1.98/+2.04, -0.01 overrun at base 94.48): they follow from the public rules alone.

AMBIGUITIES (reported in full; none found that yields a second reading the graders would punish with certainty):
(1) Money entry unit. rules:83-84 says 'Amounts and unit counts must be nonnegative integers in their stored units. Reject negative, fractional ... inputs', which literally reads as integer-cent input; rules:511-512 lists 'money with more than two decimal places' as malformed, implying dollar entry with up to two decimals, and rules:75 says money is 'Shown as' dollars and cents. No line states the unit an operator types. The dollar reading is the stronger one after reading section 12, but the two passages are not reconciled. Graders type dollar values (functional/prompt.md:17 'Money examples below are DOLLARS; app request representations may be cents'; judge.toml:1010 'Adapt dollars/cents ... to the actual UI-observed request'), which covers requests but does not tell the judge to convert for a cents-labelled input.
(2) instruction.md:11 'their what-if leaves nothing behind on the desk' against rules:544-546 (unsent entries persist per person per browser, for 'someone'). Reconciled by rules:540 'A person's own unsent entries ... are not such a record'; hro_whatif_roles (judge.toml:1361) excuses them and E1 (judge.toml:1370) tests only Finance, so either reading for non-Finance roles is graded the same.
(3) rules:60 'Nothing in this app reads the operating system's clock' against the 15-second live update and 'since the preview was saved' ordering (rules:454, 519-520). Achievable with timers and a monotonic sequence; no criterion I read demands an operation timestamp (functional/prompt.md:73 'No separate operation-timestamp field is required'). A cautious builder may hesitate, but no reading fails.
(4) rules:439-440 does not list approval-band basis among saved-preview figures while rules:498-499 says editor figures 'equal what the saved preview shows'; hro D1 (judge.toml:1307) compares only 'every figure that both the editor and the saved preview display', so both readings pass.
(5) Per-tab sessions versus 'signed out in another tab' (rules:546): hro_pol_session_resume explicitly allows the first page's own sign-out, so a per-tab-session app is not mis-graded.

What the task does well: section 12 states acceptable mechanisms (rules:499-501, 532-533, 549), route/label freedom is explicit (rules:53, 436-437) and the criteria respect it.

Not measured: no configured judge run or alternative-implementation run exists; item (1) is a source-reading finding only.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated failure. Plausible conforming alternative at risk: an app that follows rules:83-84 literally and labels its compensation inputs in integer cents (rejecting '98.23' as fractional). It still satisfies the D4 refusal (4.045 is fractional), but a judge typing the prompt's dollar literals (functional/prompt.md:63 'base98.23') without converting would see refusals across B1/D1/P3-P8. Whether the configured judge converts for a cents-labelled field is unmeasured. Weak-app direction: none found for this row.
suggested_fix: Add one sentence to hireops_rules.md section 1 (near line 83) or section 9: operators type money as dollars with at most two decimal places and the server stores integer cents; then rules:83-84 clearly governs stored values and API safe-integer limits rather than the form unit.
